description: Cross-binding conformance for a caller's `const_arrays` entry that supplies a SHAPED parameter's value (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.32.5). Such an entry is the same binding as an inline-array `parameter_overrides` entry for the parameter, so its key resolves by the same esm-spec §6.6.2 rules: the flattened name (`Column.k`) and the model-local name (`k`) both designate the parameter. Julia and Python matched the flattened name only. With no `default`, Julia refused the document with `E_TREEWALK_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE` (the parameter backed by nothing) and Python bound it as a scalar and failed the per-cell read with 'index applied to scalar value'; with a scalar `default`, both silently used the default and ignored the caller's array. Rust resolved both spellings. Each case builds the fixture through `esm_problem` with the listed `const_arrays` under every listed compiler and reads the state-free observed back through `observed_field`; the values are exact, so the comparison is exact.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no esm_problem or observed_field
scope_excluded.typescript: no esm_problem with a const-array channel

cases.note: the flattened name: the spelling every binding already accepted
the model-local name designates Column.k (esm-spec §6.6.2 rule 3)
caller data outranks the declared default under the local spelling too; a binding that missed the key reads [2, 2, 2]
